data.narrative:
Floodbase is a Series A climate and energy company founded by Bessie Schwarz and Dr. Beth Tellman. The valuation assessment draws from a broader Climate & Energy comp universe of 9 private peers and 1 public comparable (LNZA), though a sufficiently narrow same-stage peer set was unavailable to support conventional peer-median analysis.

Stage-progression methodology applies a 2.0x multiplier to the $17M total capital raised to date, yielding an implied valuation of $34M. This approach reflects typical step-up multiples observed in the progression from Series A to subsequent institutional rounds within the sector. Peer-median triangulation was not applicable; while the Climate & Energy sector contains comparable businesses—including names such as Helion, Redwood Materials, QuantumScape, KoBold Metals, and Electric Hydrogen—fewer than three peers met the narrow filters of same-stage, adjacent-stage, and similar-valuation-tier positioning. Median peer data at broader sector levels would introduce material selection bias.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $29M (low) to $39M (high), with a central estimate of $34M. This range reflects the single applicable method and the limited granularity available from the immediate peer set. Key uncertainties include the absence of same-stage comparables in climate tech and the degree to which the 2.0x step-up multiplier reflects Floodbase's specific growth profile and market position relative to earlier-stage raises. Additional financial performance data and closer peer-stage alignment would narrow this range materially.
